```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has stronger evidence that people will pay. Multiple live competitors publish self-serve prices from $19 to $749 per month (Agentshield, SealGate, OpenGuardrails, Retrace), all with URLs. That shows small teams pay for this without procurement, which suits a single paying customer within 90 days. B's anchor is mostly Ello's $14.99/mo, against a fully free, well-resourced incumbent (Khan Academy Kids) that sets a hard price ceiling.",
    "A's demand evidence is direct and on-target: two cited developer quotes describing the exact pain (fear of destructive agent actions, the need for approvals and audit trails) plus a cited public incident of an agent deleting a production database. B's strongest-looking demand quote is a parent declining to pay $500/month, which shows price resistance rather than willingness to pay.",
    "A's acquisition channel is near-zero cost, specified, and cited (Show HN / open-source launch). B's zero-cost channel, parenting communities, is explicitly marked unsourced. Its sourced channel, paid mobile UA at $2.50-$5.00 CPI in North America, is hard to justify at a sub-$15/month price for a single operator.",
    "A one-person operator running AI agents is closer to A's buyers (developers running agents) and can reach them directly. B targets parents of children aged 4-9, where trust builds over months. B also faces COPPA verifiable-consent obligations that must be in place before any launch, which adds legal setup inside the build window.",
    "Both ideas face crowded fields and trust barriers. A's barriers (SOC 2, the bar for gating destructive actions in production) mainly block enterprise tiers. B's barriers (COPPA, efficacy scrutiny, child-product trust) block the very first sale."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's main low-cost acquisition path, organic parenting communities (r/daddit, r/homeschool, r/Parenting), is explicitly marked [unsourced cost], with reach and conversion unproven. B's economics depend on this channel because paid UA at $2.50-$5.00 CPI does not work at ~$15/month. A close second: the 'parents pay tutors $25-$120/hour' figure used in B's Case For has no URL.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with free incumbents and admit the ideas lack a clear differentiating niche. A also has gaps. Its claim that buyers expect SOC 2, GDPR/DPA, and EU AI Act evidence packs carries no citation, so its severity for small self-serve buyers is unclear. Nine-plus competitors, including free OSS options, could cap willingness to pay. A wins on sourced payment evidence and a cheap channel, not because it is clearly a strong bet."
}
```
